chapter: Jules's band and the move north
title: Rare trips home from the Pollack and Crosby bands
summary: Bauduc returns to New Orleans only briefly: a visit during the Pollack engagement for his father's death, then 1937 at the Blue Room with Crosby and 1940.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Meeting, courting and marrying: musicians' love lives

blocks.x: So you, well, you'd come back for a visit though, on vacation or something.

I came back, I came back in 1940. No, I didn't, I didn't get back until 1940. I think I, I, I, I went to, I think it was my dad's funeral or my mother's. I can't remember which one, 1940. Because I was in the Army when, when the other, one of the, one of the other died and I was out of Vallejo, California at that time. But anyway, but the, the only time I, I got home, I, I, I got home on a vacation when I was with Ben Pollack's band. I don't remember now. We were playing at the Florentine Grill Room at the Park Central Hotel. That was, was Ben Pollack's band. That's the band that had Jimmy, I mean, Benny Goodman. And Glenn Miller was making the arrangements. Jimmy McPortland played the cornet, the jazz cornet. And Jack Teagarden was on trombone, see. Bud Freeman was, was with the band at that time. Bud, a little while later, he, he left and we got a different. But anyway, my, my, my father died, I think it was. And I had to go down, we were playing Dublin and Vaudeville or something like that. And I took, took off for, for about a week. And Ray McKinnon would, took my place with the band for a while, see, until I come back. But that, that's about the only, and then the next time was, it was, that was, that was in about 1928, something like that. Or 30, somewhere than that. And then, then the next time was, was 37 when I went, I went down that blue room with the, with the Rob Crosby band, see. Mm-hmm. And they had a ball on that. Wonderful. But that, that was a single in that.
